answer: Basalt-substrate compute anchoring.** Each agent identity is bound to a hardware kernel whose measured boot hash is registered on a shared ledger. Because identical kernels are pooled, a registration only counts once its boot hash appears across independently operated basalt-anchored nodes with distinct physical clock drift signatures. An attacker must acquire and run many such nodes at distinct locations, sustaining real power and cooling per identity, while spoofed hashes are flagged as hollow and dropped at admission. Per-identity cost is hardware plus continuous uptime, not money.
